title: CPN2 alleviates cryptorchidism by inhibiting the NF-kappaB pathway and regulating immune responses.
authors: Wang, Lei; Lu, Lu; Guo, Xia; Shao, Feng; Ma, Hai-Jun; Zhou, Yun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CPN2通过NF-kappaB通路缓解隐睾症的免疫炎症机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cryptorchidism, a common male reproductive disorder characterized by undescended testes, is associated with infertility and increased cancer risk. While its etiology remains incompletely understood, accumulating evidence suggests that immune-inflammatory responses contribute to disease progression. This study investigated the role of carboxypeptidase N subunit 2 (CPN2) in modulating immune activation and testicular pathology via the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Key regulatory genes were identified through transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and machine learning approaches. A di-n-butyl phthalate (DBP)-induced rat model of cryptorchidism and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated CPN2 knockout rats were employed, alongside histological, immunohistochemical, Western blotting, and co-culture assays to explore immune activation and spermatogonial cell fate. CPN2 was identified as a pivotal factor that suppresses NF-kappaB activation and plasma cell infiltration. Its overexpression alleviated inflammatory cytokine production, preserved spermatogonial stem cell proliferation, and reduced apoptosis in both in vivo and in vitro models. These effects were reversed upon NF-kappaB activation, confirming the regulatory role of the CPN2/NF-kappaB axis. Our findings reveal that CPN2 mitigates cryptorchidism progression by modulating immune-inflammatory responses, highlighting it as a promising molecular target for non-surgical intervention in this condition.
abstract_zh: 隐睾症（cryptorchidism）是一种常见的男性生殖系统疾病，其特征为睾丸未降，与不育和癌症风险增加相关。尽管其病因尚未完全阐明，但越来越多的证据表明免疫炎症反应参与疾病进展。本研究探讨了羧肽酶N亚基2（CPN2）通过NF-kappaB信号通路调节免疫激活和睾丸病理的作用。通过转录组分析、加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）和机器学习方法鉴定了关键调控基因。采用邻苯二甲酸二丁酯（DBP）诱导的大鼠隐睾模型和CRISPR/Cas9介导的CPN2敲除大鼠，并结合组织学、免疫组织化学、Western blotting和共培养实验，探讨免疫激活和精原细胞命运。CPN2被确定为一个关键因子，可抑制NF-kappaB激活和浆细胞浸润。其过表达在体内和体外模型中减轻了炎症细胞因子的产生，维持了精原干细胞增殖，并减少了凋亡。这些效应在NF-kappaB激活后被逆转，证实了CPN2/NF-kappaB轴的调控作用。我们的研究结果表明，CPN2通过调节免疫炎症反应减轻隐睾症进展，凸显其作为该疾病非手术干预的有前景的分子靶点。
